en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn what comes after verbs like want and enjoy, and how to say why you do something. Let's go one small step at a time.

steps.title: Two verbs together: want to
steps.text: Sometimes two verbs come together: I want + go home. Let's see how English joins them.
steps.body: A **verb** is an action word: *go, eat, buy*. When two verbs meet, the **first verb decides** the form of the second. After **want, need, would like, hope, plan, decide, learn**, use **to + base form** (the plain verb from the dictionary, no -s, no -ing): I want **to go** home. Indonesian says *mau pulang* with nothing in between, but English needs **to**: not `I want go home`. Only the first verb takes -s: Rina **wants to go**, not `wants to goes`.

steps.title: Wants, needs and plans
steps.text: Here are some real sentences. Look for the to after the first verb.
steps.body: Negative: **don't / doesn't want to**. Question: **Do you need to ...?** After to, always the base form.

examples.en: I want to go home.
examples.id: Saya mau pulang.

examples.en: We need to leave at seven.
examples.id: Kami perlu berangkat jam tujuh.

examples.en: Sari hopes to work in Singapore one day.
examples.id: Sari berharap bisa bekerja di Singapura suatu hari nanti.

examples.en: Every year, many people decide to learn English.
examples.id: Setiap tahun, banyak orang memutuskan untuk belajar bahasa Inggris.

examples.en: Rina doesn't want to cook tonight.
examples.id: Rina tidak mau masak malam ini.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Let's try one. What comes after need?

question.prompt: My laptop is very old. Complete: I need ___ a new one.
question.explanation: need is followed by **to + base form**: I need **to buy** a new one. Without to (`I need buy`) is the Indonesian *perlu beli* pattern, and need doesn't take -ing here.

steps.title: Verb + -ing: enjoy, finish, don't mind
steps.text: Now the other list: verbs that want -ing after them.
steps.body: After **enjoy** (senang, menikmati), **finish** (selesai) and **don't mind** (tidak keberatan), use **verb + -ing**: I enjoy **swimming**. Not `I enjoy to swim`: these verbs never take to. **like, love, hate** can take both: *I like swimming* = *I like to swim*. But **would like** takes only to: I'd like **to** swim. There's no rule you can see, so **memorise the two lists**: learn each verb with its partner (*want to, enjoy -ing*).

pairs.en: When I finish eating, I wash my plate.
pairs.id: Kalau sudah selesai makan, saya mencuci piring saya.

pairs.en: My mother doesn't mind cooking for ten people.
pairs.id: Ibu saya tidak keberatan memasak untuk sepuluh orang.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Which form comes after enjoy?

question.prompt: Sari loves books. Complete: She enjoys ___ before bed.
question.explanation: enjoy is followed by **verb + -ing**: She enjoys **reading**. `enjoys to read` is a very common mistake, because Indonesian *senang membaca* doesn't change the verb.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Your friend is late and says sorry. Tell her it's OK.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Tidak apa-apa, saya tidak keberatan menunggu kamu.
question.solution: I don't mind waiting for you.
question.explanation: **don't mind** (tidak keberatan) is followed by **-ing**: don't mind **waiting**. *wait for* = menunggu.

steps.title: to = untuk: saying why
steps.text: Last part: how to say why you do something.
steps.body: To say **why** you do something, use **to + base form**: I go to the bank **to get** money. It answers *Why?*: Why do you go to the bank? — **To get** money. Indonesian *untuk* makes many learners say `for get money`. But **for** comes before a **noun**, a thing (*for lunch, for my son*), and **to** before a **verb**. Two to's in one sentence? *to the bank* = **ke**, *to get* = **untuk**.

steps.title: Why? To ...
steps.text: Here are some reasons. Look at to + verb, and at for + noun in the last one.

examples.en: Pak Hasan works on Saturdays to earn extra money.
examples.id: Pak Hasan bekerja hari Sabtu untuk mendapat uang tambahan.

examples.en: Rina is learning English to get a job in a hotel.
examples.id: Rina sedang belajar bahasa Inggris untuk mendapat pekerjaan di hotel.

examples.en: Why do you get up at five? — To catch the first train.
examples.id: Kenapa kamu bangun jam lima? — Untuk naik kereta pertama.

examples.en: I go to the warung for lunch.
examples.id: Saya ke warung untuk makan siang.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Bu Ani's son is sick. Why does she go to the pharmacy?

question.prompt: Complete: Bu Ani goes to the pharmacy ___ medicine for her son.
question.explanation: This says **why** she goes, so use **to + base form**: to get. `for get` comes from *untuk*, but for goes before a noun (like *for her son*), not before a verb.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Budi wants a motorbike. Say why he saves money.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Budi menabung untuk membeli motor.
question.solution: Budi saves money to buy a motorbike.
question.explanation: First what Budi does (**saves money**), then why: **to + base form** (*to buy* = untuk membeli). *saves money* = menabung.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here is everything on one page. Keep it and learn the two lists.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Verb + to / verb + -ing
artifact.intro: The first verb decides the form of the second: to + base form or -ing. Learn each verb with its partner.
rows: he / she: -s on the first verb only
I don't want to cook tonight.
Saya tidak mau masak malam ini.
I like swimming. = I like to swim.
I go to the bank to get money.
Saya ke bank untuk mengambil uang.
I go to the warung for lunch.
Saya ke warung untuk makan siang.
tips: No rule to see: learn each verb with its partner, **want to**, **enjoy -ing**.
*untuk* + verb = **to**, not `for`: I go to the bank **to get** money.
After to, always the base form: She wants to **go**, not `to goes`.

examples.id: Kami perlu berangkat jam tujuh.

examples.en: Dimas enjoys playing football with his friends.
examples.id: Dimas senang bermain sepak bola dengan teman-temannya.

examples.en: Why do you get up at five? — To catch the first train.
examples.id: Kenapa kamu bangun jam lima? — Untuk naik kereta pertama.

steps.text: Want more? This video and these two pages explain verbs + to, verbs + -ing and to for purpose, with short tests.

id.greeting: Halo! Hari ini kamu akan belajar apa yang datang setelah kata kerja seperti want dan enjoy, dan cara menjelaskan kenapa kamu melakukan sesuatu. Kita pelajari pelan-pelan, satu langkah kecil setiap kali.

steps.title: Dua kata kerja berurutan: want to
steps.text: Kadang dua kata kerja muncul berurutan: I want + go home. Yuk lihat cara bahasa Inggris menggabungkannya.
steps.body: **Kata kerja** adalah kata untuk kegiatan: *go, eat, buy*. Kalau dua kata kerja bertemu, **kata kerja pertama menentukan** bentuk kata kerja kedua. Setelah **want, need, would like, hope, plan, decide, learn**, pakai **to + bentuk dasar** (kata kerja polos seperti di kamus, tanpa -s, tanpa -ing): I want **to go** home. Bahasa Indonesia bilang *mau pulang* tanpa kata di tengahnya, tapi bahasa Inggris perlu **to**: bukan `I want go home`. Hanya kata kerja pertama yang diberi -s: Rina **wants to go**, bukan `wants to goes`.

steps.title: Keinginan, kebutuhan dan rencana
steps.text: Ini beberapa kalimat nyata. Cari to setelah kata kerja pertama.
steps.body: Negatif: **don't / doesn't want to**. Pertanyaan: **Do you need to ...?** Setelah to, selalu bentuk dasar.

examples.id: Saya mau pulang.

examples.en: We need to leave at seven.
examples.id: Kami perlu berangkat jam tujuh.

examples.id: Sari berharap bisa bekerja di Singapura suatu hari nanti.

examples.id: Setiap tahun, banyak orang memutuskan untuk belajar bahasa Inggris.

examples.id: Rina tidak mau masak malam ini.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Yuk coba satu. Apa yang datang setelah need?

question.prompt: Laptop-ku sudah sangat tua. Lengkapi: I need ___ a new one.
question.explanation: need diikuti **to + bentuk dasar**: I need **to buy** a new one. Tanpa to (`I need buy`) itu pola bahasa Indonesia *perlu beli*, dan need tidak memakai -ing di sini.

steps.title: Kata kerja + -ing: enjoy, finish, don't mind
steps.text: Sekarang daftar yang lain: kata kerja yang diikuti -ing.
steps.body: Setelah **enjoy** (senang, menikmati), **finish** (selesai) dan **don't mind** (tidak keberatan), pakai **kata kerja + -ing**: I enjoy **swimming**. Bukan `I enjoy to swim`: kata kerja ini tidak pernah memakai to. **like, love, hate** bisa memakai keduanya: *I like swimming* = *I like to swim*. Tapi **would like** hanya memakai to: I'd like **to** swim. Tidak ada aturan yang kelihatan, jadi **hafalkan dua daftar ini**: pelajari setiap kata kerja bersama pasangannya (*want to, enjoy -ing*).

pairs.en: When I finish eating, I wash my plate.
pairs.id: Kalau sudah selesai makan, saya mencuci piring saya.

pairs.en: My mother doesn't mind cooking for ten people.
pairs.id: Ibu saya tidak keberatan memasak untuk sepuluh orang.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Bentuk apa yang datang setelah enjoy?

question.prompt: Sari suka buku. Lengkapi: She enjoys ___ before bed.
question.explanation: enjoy diikuti **kata kerja + -ing**: She enjoys **reading**. `enjoys to read` adalah kesalahan yang sangat umum, karena *senang membaca* dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak mengubah kata kerjanya.

steps.title: Susun kalimat
steps.text: Temanmu terlambat dan minta maaf. Bilang bahwa tidak apa-apa.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Tidak apa-apa, saya tidak keberatan menunggu kamu.
question.solution: I don't mind waiting for you.
question.explanation: **don't mind** (tidak keberatan) diikuti **-ing**: don't mind **waiting**. *wait for* = menunggu.

steps.title: to = untuk: menjelaskan tujuan
steps.text: Bagian terakhir: cara bilang kenapa kamu melakukan sesuatu.
steps.body: Untuk bilang **kenapa** kamu melakukan sesuatu, pakai **to + bentuk dasar**: I go to the bank **to get** money. Ini menjawab *Why?*: Why do you go to the bank? — **To get** money. Kata *untuk* membuat banyak orang bilang `for get money`. Padahal **for** dipakai sebelum **kata benda**, yaitu benda (*for lunch, for my son*), dan **to** sebelum **kata kerja**. Ada dua to dalam satu kalimat? *to the bank* = **ke**, *to get* = **untuk**.

steps.title: Why? To ...
steps.text: Ini beberapa alasan. Perhatikan to + kata kerja, dan for + kata benda di contoh terakhir.

examples.id: Rina sedang belajar bahasa Inggris untuk mendapat pekerjaan di hotel.

examples.en: Why do you get up at five? — To catch the first train.
examples.id: Kenapa kamu bangun jam lima? — Untuk naik kereta pertama.

examples.en: I go to the warung for lunch.
examples.id: Saya ke warung untuk makan siang.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Anak Bu Ani sakit. Kenapa dia pergi ke apotek?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Bu Ani goes to the pharmacy ___ medicine for her son.
question.explanation: Ini menjelaskan **kenapa** dia pergi, jadi pakai **to + bentuk dasar**: to get. `for get` datang dari kata *untuk*, padahal for dipakai sebelum kata benda (seperti *for her son*), bukan sebelum kata kerja.

steps.title: Susun kalimat
steps.text: Budi ingin punya motor. Bilang kenapa dia menabung.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Budi menabung untuk membeli motor.
question.solution: Budi saves money to buy a motorbike.
question.explanation: Pertama apa yang Budi lakukan (**saves money**), lalu kenapa: **to + bentuk dasar** (*to buy* = untuk membeli). *saves money* = menabung.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan dan hafalkan dua daftarnya, ya.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · Kata kerja + to / kata kerja + -ing
artifact.intro: Kata kerja pertama menentukan bentuk kata kerja kedua: to + bentuk dasar atau -ing. Hafalkan setiap kata kerja bersama pasangannya.
rows: he / she: -s hanya di kata kerja pertama
I don't want to cook tonight.
Saya tidak mau masak malam ini.
I like swimming. = I like to swim.
I go to the bank to get money.
Saya ke bank untuk mengambil uang.
I go to the warung for lunch.
Saya ke warung untuk makan siang.
tips: Tidak ada aturan yang kelihatan: hafalkan setiap kata kerja bersama pasangannya, **want to**, **enjoy -ing**.
*untuk* + kata kerja = **to**, bukan `for`: I go to the bank **to get** money.
Setelah to, selalu bentuk dasar: She wants to **go**, bukan `to goes`.
